craft_notes: Sthāyin: conviction-removes (niścaya undoes what niścaya did: I-mine-this are conviction's DOING). Sanskrit: ahaṃ mameti...niścayakaraṇam...nirāśrayaṃ mano yāti...dhyāna...śamam → L4 keeps quoted-three line 1, supportless-goes-calm line 2. Rows: row 3 (impulse→calm). Close: calm (śama — supportless mind GOES to calm: motion into stillness). Rejected: 'ego' — killed: I-mine-this kept (the three quoted words ARE the verse); 'letting go' — killed: goes kept (the mind's motion, not a release).

lines: supportless mind goes — meditation's impulse, calm.
l4.sanskrit_cite: ahaṃ mamedam ityādi pratipattiprasaṅgataḥ | nirādhāre mano yāti taddhyānapreraṇāc chamī

reads_against.argmap: How does conviction free the mind? → Conviction removes I-mine; supportless mind falls into calm.
reads_against.c1_rasa: śānta with vīra undertow (stillness that ends in sovereignty)
